Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

School & learning

educational adjective

that teaches something

also instructive, educational film, educational toy, educational game

* our formation

* (our own formation) ad discendum ūtilis

phrase: ūtilis with ad and the gerund

educational, useful for learning

A plain description in a classical construction (ūtilis ad with a gerund or noun); ad docendum aptus says the same from the teacher’s side.

Other words

  • didascalicus, didascalica, didascalicum — educational, didactic

    declension · also used · modern · Traupman 52: pellicula didascalica, educational film

    Greek διδασκαλικός; ante- and post-classical and rare (Didascalica, the title of a work by Accius; Ausonius): Lewis & Short.

Examples

  • Hic lūdus et jūcundus est et ad discendum ūtilis.

    This game is fun and educational.composed

See also education, learn, teach.

SourcesLewis & Short: utilis · Lewis & Short: didascalicus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 52.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
